data.narrative:
Koloma is a Series B climate and energy technology company founded by Tom Darrah, Pete Johnson, and Paul Harraka. The company has raised $245M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer set of 9 comparable companies—1 public and 8 private—including KoBold Metals, Redwood Materials, Helion, Electric Hydrogen, and Amogy, primarily at Series C stage.

Two triangulation methods are applied. The stage-progression approach uses total capital raised ($245M) as a proxy for current valuation and applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B advancement, yielding $466M. The peer-median method relies on three same-sector comparables at Series C stage—KoBold Metals ($3.0B), Electric Hydrogen ($1.0B), and Amogy ($700M)—with a median valuation of $1.0B.

Synthesizing both methods produces a triangulated range of $396M (low), $733M (median), to $1.1B (high). The median of $733M sits midway between the stage-progression result and peer median, reflecting the tension between Koloma's earlier stage (Series B) relative to peer benchmarks (Series C). Key uncertainties include sensitivity to peer selection within the Climate & Energy sector and the applicability of stage-progression multipliers given sector-specific capital intensity and commercialization timelines.
